$comment: Rails for the verifier's ORCHESTRATOR session, added by `ralph.sh` with
`--settings` because `roles.ts` names this file as the role's
`orchestratorSettings`, INSTEAD of the harness-wide
`claude-orchestrator-settings.json` — so it repeats every rule of that
file, and adds the verifier's own.
The verifier checks acceptance criteria against PRODUCTION
(felipearos/ralph#566). It may never write to a database, so every
database client is denied: read-only SQL goes through
`verifier/acceptance.ts sql`, which opens a read-only transaction on the
project's read-only connection and always rolls back. It acts in
production only as the test account, which `verifier/acceptance.ts`
signs in for it, so `curl` and `wget` are denied too: a request crafted
by hand could carry some other account's token, and would skip the
tool's redaction. Nor may it edit the watch store
(`ralph/verifier-watches.json` in git's common directory), whose
evidence and decisions only the gate and `verifier/checkin.ts` write.
Nor does it write code, in any mode (#568). Act mode's revert is the
GATE's: it reverts in a scratch worktree, pushes the verifier's own
branch, opens the revert PR and merges it only through the project's
`verifier.mergeCommand`, all outside this session. So the session may not
edit a file, commit, revert, push, open or merge a pull request, or reach
GitHub's API raw (`gh api` can merge and push as well as read). It still
writes NEW files under `.ralph/logs/` (its acceptance results and journal
draft) with `Write`, so `Write` stays open and the role's clean-detached
invariant is what catches a stray file in the checkout.
Both spellings, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`, for the reason
`claude-executor-settings.json` gives. A tripwire, not the boundary: the
boundary is that the session holds no credential — the test account's
and the read-only connection's stay in the ui-shots store it is denied
below — and that the read-only connection is read-only in the database.
